thread:
Morgan: Heads-up — we started a canary for session-cache-ttl in prod. Quick question: who is allowed to flip the emergency toggle for session-cache (prod) if we see a regression? Also what exact audit/notification steps do we need? cc @alex @riley

Alex: I thought flips are restricted to oncall + platform leads, but our runbook might be stale. We should make it explicit (who can flip, how to document, where logs land).

Riley: Runbook currently says 'sre-oncall' or 'platform-lead' can flip, but that doc predates the admin console. We need an API snippet + one-click console flow. @morgan can you capture minimal steps?

SRE Bot: AUTO: Any feature-flag change in prod must include an incident/link and a human-readable comment. Change will be logged to feature-flips.audit_table.

Morgan: Draft proposal (short checklist):
1) Create an incident in Jira if users impacted (label: session-cache).
2) Post to #incidents and ping oncall + platform leads.
3) Flip toggle via admin console OR API (preferred for scripts).
4) Add comment with reason + incident/Jira link.
5) Verify metrics (error_rate, p95 latency, cache-hit-rate) for 10m.
6) If stable, document in postmortem; if not, rollback and escalate to Eng Director.

Jamie: Add escalation rules: if after flip error_rate > threshold for 10m, page @devon and escalate pager duty. Also require 2FA on console flips and an explicit 'rollback plan' note.

Devon: +1. Also: require that flips only set the flag to safe states (eg: 'off' or 'limited') — no experimental modes. Audit entry must include who flipped, timestamp, and rationale.

Alex: Example API call (put in runbook):
```bash
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/toggles/session-cache \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"state":"off","comment":"rollback due to increased errors - incident: SESS-123"}'
```
After call, check /api/v1/flags/session-cache/history for the entry.

Morgan: I'll add this to the SRE runbook and Confluence page. Plan: I won't flip anything until the incident is logged and the console/API audit path is verified.

Ops Rotation Bot: Reminder: Oncall today: Morgan. If you flip the flag, please update the rotation notes and mark the action.

Riley: One more guardrail: require a canary audience cutoff first (move 100% -> 0% via rollout audiences) rather than toggling global off when possible. If global flip is necessary, document why the canary failed.

Jamie: I'll update the runbook section with the checklist and add the curl snippet + console screenshot. Tagging @morgan when done. :thumbsup:

Morgan: Thanks all — I'll create the Jira incident now and link back here before any flips.
